title: Check yourself: Clear, direct instructions, context and roles

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A prompt says "Condense the contract, but don't be too long." Outputs range from one line to two pages. Which revision best fixes the inconsistency?

options.text: Cap it at five bullets, each under twenty words
options.says: A measurable constraint is clear and direct and can be checked afterwards (the clear and direct section).

options.text: Add "be concise, thorough and precise" so every summary stays focused
options.says: Ruled out because stacking adjectives "gives conflicting, unverifiable demands" (the first trap).

options.text: Open with "You are a senior contracts lawyer" to set the right length
options.says: Ruled out because "A role sets vocabulary, depth, tone and what to pay attention to", not a length that was never stated.

options.text: Restate "keep it reasonably short" as the last line after the contract
options.says: Ruled out because restating only helps the model find the task: the page's rule is to "restate the task after a long block of material", and "reasonably short" is still an unmeasured demand.

questions.stem: An application prompt says "Never mention competitors." Users who ask for feature comparisons still sometimes get a rival brand in the reply. Which change best follows the page's guidance?

options.text: Put the rule in capitals and add "this is critical, never break it" to stress it
options.says: Ruled out because emphasis adds no reason, and "The second explains itself and generalises", which a shouted rule does not.

options.text: Move the rule into a role line: "You are a loyal brand ambassador"
options.says: Ruled out because "A role is a request, not a credential", and a role changes the voice, not the obligation.

options.text: Add the reason, for example that legal advice bars naming other firms
options.says: A rule with its reason lets the model apply it to cases the rule did not list (the purpose and context section, with the text-to-speech example).

options.text: Soften it to "try to avoid competitors where practical"
options.says: Ruled out because the page contrasts "It would be great if the answer were short" with a firm instruction, so a softer rule gives the model less to generalise from.

origin.section: Give the purpose and the context
